metadata.title: TIMSS 2019 U.S. Results
metadata.venue: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics

extraction.outcome_summary: The report presented descriptive TIMSS 2019 results for U.S. 4th- and 8th-graders in mathematics and science, comparing average scores, percentile gaps, benchmark attainment, and trends over time. It showed that U.S. students generally scored above the international average, but score gaps between top and bottom performers were relatively large and had widened in several cases. Boys outperformed girls in 4th-grade mathematics and science, while gender differences at grade 8 were mostly not significant. The report also highlighted substantial differences by race/ethnicity and school poverty, with higher achievement in lower-poverty schools and lower achievement in higher-poverty schools.
